messages:
rui.z: Strange deadlock hit in our Android sample today. Lots of concurrent uploads + auth refresh = everything stalls. Repro notes below.

rui.z: Repro: Android 8 emulator, okhttp 4.10.0, Retrofit 2.9. We batch-start ~20 upload calls concurrently. Each call uses the shared OkHttpClient (default Dispatcher). When a token expires mid-upload the Authenticator tries to refresh (synchronously) but that refresh call itself uses the same client. Result: refresh request queues behind maxRequestsPerHost and never executes -> uploads hang.

anya.k: Oh yeah that's the classic "Authenticator uses same dispatcher" deadlock. OkHttp Dispatcher defaults are maxRequests=64 and maxRequestsPerHost=5, so if many blocked calls occupy per-host slots the authenticator's internal call can get queued. On older Android devices/emulators thread scheduling makes it worse.

sam.h: We saw a similar one in server SDK a while back. Fix was to make the Authenticator use a dedicated OkHttpClient with an isolated Dispatcher (or use a blocking sync token store that talks to a different client). Two patterns: (A) have TokenStore.refresh use a small client with maxRequestsPerHost=1 and its own connection pool, or (B) perform refresh on a dedicated executor and bypass Dispatcher queuing entirely.

rui.z: Proof: with logging we saw Authenticator.authenticate() invoked, then TokenStore.refresh() attempted to execute a retrofit call and that call never left the queue because all 5 per-host slots are held by blocked uploads.

anya.k: Workarounds: 
- short term: lower concurrency for uploads or increase maxRequestsPerHost on the shared Dispatcher (but that affects other traffic).
- recommended: create an internal refreshClient: `OkHttpClient.Builder().dispatcher(Dispatcher(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor())).retryOnConnectionFailure(true).build()` and use that for token refresh only.

sam.h: Code sketch we used: 
```
val refreshClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()))
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(2, 5, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
  .build()

class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    synchronized(tokenLock) {
      val fresh = TokenStore.getOrRefresh(refreshClient)
      return response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $fresh").build()
    }
  }
}
```

anya.k: Note: don't call back into the same OkHttpClient from your Authenticator. Also don't perform long blocking work on OkHttp's internal threads. Use a tiny client or offload to a different executor to avoid starving the dispatcher.

rui.z: Implemented refreshClient approach in sample app and re-ran 50 concurrent uploads on Android 8 emulator. Deadlock gone. On Android 11 it previously didn't reproduce as often.

ci-bot: test-run 2245679000: android-upload-concurrency (rui.z) -> flaky(5/10) before patch, 0/10 after patch.

sam.h: For SDK: add a note in the Android samples and SDK migration guide: "Authenticator must not synchronously call the same client it authenticates. Use a dedicated refresh client or serialized refresh with a different dispatcher." Add the refreshClient code snippet.

anya.k: Also add a short lint-like runtime check in the sample builder: if TokenStore.refresh is null or uses the default client, log a warning when concurrentRequests > 8 (heuristic) to help devs surface this config.

rui.z: I'll open a small PR to: (1) add refreshClient snippet to samples, (2) include a short explanation in docs, (3) add the runtime warning. After that I'll run the emulator matrix across API 26/28/30.

release-bot: deploy 2245679010 started: devex-samples: auth-dispatcher-fix (rui.z) :rocket:

rui.z: Thanks everyone . Leaving thread open for QA results and doc wording review.
